subject: core-gate-harness-specifications.v1
role: The authoring act for the five already-named core gate harness identifiers — the OBL-2 leftover that D-160 recorded as open on DR-101, and the first artifact in this series that authors specifications rather than measuring what is owed.
verdictRule: ACCEPT only at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX. Measured: 0 blockers, 1 SHOULD-FIX. The rule is not discretionary, so the verdict is REJECT.
acceptanceGrade: REJECT-ON-ONE-FIELD. The substance is strong and I could not break it: every threshold, machine, rank and protocol clause traces to D-006 or D-102 verbatim, and the arithmetic is right. One field named claimVerbatim is not verbatim.

d006Thresholds: G01 ≤ 25 MB per platform — matches D-006 clause 1.
G02 ≤ 80 MB installed, inventory enumerated, zero undeclared dependencies as DR-126's qualitative half — matches clause 2 and v16's ID-DEP-K2.
G03 cold p50 ≤ 100 / p95 ≤ 150 / p99 ≤ 250 ms, warm p95 ≤ 50 / p99 ≤ 100 ms, loads no components or project — matches clause 3, all five percentiles.

G04 help/version steady ≤ 40 MB, peak ≤ 50 MB — matches clause 4. The doctor read-only pair, steady ≤ 60 MB and peak ≤ 100 MB, is also D-006's own numeral from clause 4's turn-2 NOTE-04, not an invention; I checked this specifically because a fifth and sixth number is exactly where an invented cap would hide.

shouldFix.title: DR-G03's claimVerbatim is not verbatim: the code-span backticks around --help and --version are dropped
shouldFix.finding: The live DR-G03 claim cell reads, byte for byte, '`--help`/`--version` remain fast and load no components/project'. The artifact's claimVerbatim reads '--help/--version remain fast and load no components/project'. The four other claimVerbatim fields — G01, G02, G04 and G05 — are byte-exact against their live cells, so the deviation is specific to G03 rather than a uniform house style of stripping markup.
shouldFix.whyItMatters: The field name is a checkable promise, and this corpus treats it as one: the DR-117 naming candidates were reviewed by comparing nine such fields with equality, and the gate-harness-naming lineage carried a finding for a dropped owner parenthetical. D-157's fenced operands preserved backticks precisely because byte-exactness was the point. A later act that copies this field, or a later reviewer who diffs it against the register expecting to skip re-checking, gets a mismatch from a field that says it will not produce one.
shouldFix.whyNotBlocker: The dropped characters are markdown code-span delimiters, not semantic content. The claim's meaning is unchanged, no threshold or protocol depends on it, and nothing downstream computes on the string. This is the smallest possible instance of the defect, and I say so rather than dressing it up.
shouldFix.repair: Restore the two code spans so the value reads '`--help`/`--version` remain fast and load no components/project', matching the live cell byte for byte as the other four do.

consideredAndDeclined.item: Grading the claimVerbatim deviation an advisory instead
consideredAndDeclined.whyDeclined: I weighed it, because the dropped characters are markup and change no meaning. What decided it is that the field's name is a promise this corpus checks mechanically — I verified nine such fields with equality across the DR-117 naming reviews, and D-157's operands preserved backticks precisely because byte-exactness was the operative property. Four of five fields keep the promise here, so the deviation is a fixable slip rather than a convention.

consideredAndDeclined.item: Charging the artifact for specifying doctor read-only RSS at G04 when the gate's claim names baseline/peak generally
consideredAndDeclined.whyDeclined: D-006 clause 4 binds the gate's two quantities separately and states the doctor read-only pair explicitly, so the artifact is carrying the decision rather than widening the gate. It also repeats D-006's exclusion of analyze and consented-probe RSS and makes scoring them a fail condition.

consideredAndDeclined.item: Charging the G05 trigger statement as forward-looking product judgement
consideredAndDeclined.whyDeclined: It is D-006's own sentence about slice 1's TypeScript provider, quoted in substance, and the artifact still refuses to invent caps.

coordinatorSummary: REJECT at 0 blockers and 1 SHOULD-FIX. Sixteen attacks run, one landed, and the repair is two backtick pairs. Custody holds: subject 1db54738 at 0444 unmoved with dispatch and prompt agreeing, HEAD never left 5d5d778, file 08 at 3a9442d1 equal to the subject's own pin, governing tree clean, and all four cited digests reproduce. I also confirmed D-166 took effect: COORD now carries exactly one D-165 heading. The substance is strong and I could not break it. I derived D-006's numerals and D-102's fleet classes and protocol from their own adopted text before reading the subject, and every quantitative claim traces: 25 MB and 80 MB with byte figures 26214400 and 83886080 both exactly right; all five G03 percentiles; G04's help/version 40/50 MB and — the place an invented cap would hide, so I checked it specifically — the doctor read-only 60/100 MB pair, which is D-006 clause 4's own turn-2 NOTE-04 numeral rather than an invention; G05 measurement-and-visibility with no cap and the explicit statement that exceeding a cap cannot be a fail; and the regression rule's clause-1-to-4 domain with the first-release base case. The G05 trigger sentence is D-006's own. On D-102, the four fleet labels, their CPU and RAM figures, the Intel VM UDID, the two exclusions, N=21, the nearest-rank ranks 11/20/21, the warm-p50-is-telemetry rule and G04's every-accepted-sample absolute rule all reproduce D-102's sentences, and the artifact says it does not amend that protocol. Two defects from the DR-101 join's own history are absent here: the five gate owners are carried per gate and byte-exact rather than collapsed to the row owner, and this artifact is the authoring OBL-2 was waiting for rather than a claim that naming sufficed — its closure field is keyed leftoverDesignClosedIfAcceptedAndRecorded and it keeps gates 2 and 3 shut on OD-101-1 and OD-101-2. The objection is one field. DR-G03's claimVerbatim drops the code-span backticks around --help and --version that the live cell carries; the other four are byte-exact, so it is a slip rather than a convention. I weighed advisory and chose SHOULD-FIX because the field name is a promise this corpus checks mechanically — I verified nine such fields by equality across the DR-117 naming reviews, and D-157's operands preserved backticks precisely because byte-exactness was the operative property. It is the smallest possible instance of that defect and I say so plainly.
